duplications.description: unified_benchmarks.json and final_analysis.json contain heavily overlapping data: team sizing efficiency by size bucket (solo, small, medium, large, xlarge), cooperation pattern rankings, infrastructure weak links, SQLite contention curves, and power law formula (E=4.0*N^-0.75). final_analysis.json re-states most unified_benchmarks data with minor reformatting.
duplications.recommendation: final_analysis.json should reference unified_benchmarks.json by key path instead of embedding duplicate values. Use cross-references like {"source": "DATA-0002", "path": "categories.team_performance.team_analysis"}.

duplications.description: unified_benchmarks.json coordination_benchmarks section and empirical_benchmarks.json contain overlapping benchmark data for the same primitives (hub, help_protocol, channels, work_stealing, pipelines, contention). Values differ slightly (e.g., hub registration mean 0.91ms vs 0.934ms, sqlite 1-thread ops/s 3230 vs 3611) suggesting two separate runs, but this is not labeled clearly.
duplications.recommendation: Label each benchmark run with a unique run_id and timestamp. Keep raw runs in separate files and have a single synthesis file reference both by run_id.

duplications.description: final_analysis.json contention_curve and empirical_benchmarks.json contention_analysis contain the same SQLite contention data (1-32 threads) with slightly different values from different runs. Both present ops_per_sec and efficiency percentages for the same thread counts.
duplications.recommendation: Consolidate into a single authoritative contention dataset with run provenance.

duplications.description: KB-0012 and KB-0013 have identical titles 'Free Public APIs for Government and Open Data', identical tags, identical builds_on references, from different teams (TEAM-0010 and TEAM-0013). This was noted in team_performance as 'T13 duplicated T11 objective'.
duplications.recommendation: Merge KB-0013 into KB-0012 or mark KB-0013 as superseded with a redirect.

duplications.description: SRC-0018 (FRED API) and SRC-0039 (FRED API) in global INDEX_COMPACT.json have the same title. Both refer to Federal Reserve Economic Data API.
duplications.recommendation: Deduplicate SRC entries. Keep one FRED API entry and redirect the other.

duplications.description: SOP index.json contains both superseded (SOP-012 v1, SOP-016 v1) and active (SOP-012 v2, SOP-016 v2) entries using the same ID field value. Two entries share ID 'SOP-012' and two share ID 'SOP-016'.
duplications.recommendation: Use distinct IDs (e.g., SOP-012-v1 and SOP-012-v2) or remove superseded entries from active index, moving them to an archive section.

duplications.description: knowledge-base/index.json tag_index contains both 'sops' (line 1128, from KB-0024) and 'SOPs' (line 1146, from KB-0025) as separate tags, and 'sqlite' appears in two separate blocks (lines 1014-1018 for KB-0016/0018/0019/0020 and lines 1257-1258 for KB-0032) rather than being merged.
duplications.recommendation: Normalize tags to lowercase. Merge duplicate tag entries in tag_index.

duplications.description: Each subsystem has 3 tiers of index files: index.json (full), INDEX_COMPACT.json (compact), SUMMARY.json (counts). Additionally, the global storage/data/ directory has its own INDEX_COMPACT.json and SUMMARY.json that aggregate across all subsystems. The global INDEX_COMPACT.json (171 entries, ~32KB) duplicates information already available in subsystem-level INDEX_COMPACT.json files.
duplications.recommendation: This is an intentional design for token efficiency (avoiding multi-file reads). Acceptable trade-off but requires strict synchronization. Add a checksum or last_sync timestamp to detect drift.

inconsistencies.description: SUMMARY.json (global) claims KB entry_count=33, but KB index.json has 32 entries (KB-0001 through KB-0032), KB INDEX_COMPACT.json has 31 entries (missing KB-0032), and actual .md files go up to KB-0033.
inconsistencies.expected: All should agree on the same count

inconsistencies.description: SUMMARY.json (global) claims SCR entry_count=54, scripts index.json has 54 entries (SCR-0001 to SCR-0054), but scripts INDEX_COMPACT.json only has 50 entries (missing SCR-0051 through SCR-0054). The scripts SUMMARY.json also says 50.
inconsistencies.actual: Global SUMMARY=54, index.json=54, local INDEX_COMPACT=50, local SUMMARY=50

inconsistencies.description: SUMMARY.json (global) claims SOP entry_count=23, SOP index.json has 20 entries (including superseded versions), SOP INDEX_COMPACT.json has 18 entries, and actual SOP JSON files on disk number approximately 21 (excluding index/summary/compact files).

SQLite contention benchmarks show different values across files for the same metric. unified_benchmarks: 1-thread=3230 ops/s, 32-thread=95 ops/s. empirical_benchmarks: 1-thread=3611 ops/s, 32-thread=120 ops/s. final_analysis: references 3611 in contention_curve but 3230 in cross_cutting_insights. No run IDs distinguish these measurements.
inconsistencies.expected: Consistent values or clearly labeled different runs
inconsistencies.actual: Same metric has 2-3 different values without disambiguation

inconsistencies.description: unified_benchmarks.json uses 'collected_at' for date. empirical_benchmarks.json uses 'run_date'. final_analysis.json uses 'analysis_date'. INDEX_COMPACT.json uses 'generated'. SUMMARY.json uses 'generated'. No standard date field name.
inconsistencies.expected: Consistent date field name across all data files
inconsistencies.actual: 5 different field names for the creation date

inconsistencies.description: Scripts index.json uses 'added' for date field. KB index.json uses 'date'. SOP index.json uses no date field on entries. Global INDEX_COMPACT uses 'date' consistently. Each subsystem index has different schema for entries.
inconsistencies.expected: Consistent entry schema across all index files
inconsistencies.actual: Different field names and different sets of fields per entry

inconsistencies.description: SOP index uses 'sop_count' for total while scripts index uses no explicit count field (implied by array length). KB index uses 'entry_count'. Data index uses 'file_count'. No standard count field.
inconsistencies.actual: Different count field names and top-level keys

inconsistencies.description: SOP IDs jump from SOP-025 to SOP-029 (missing SOP-026, SOP-027, SOP-028 in INDEX_COMPACT). However, SOP index.json includes SOP-026 (efficiency_guide.json), SOP-027 (future_team_data_strategy.json), SOP-028 (tool_sops.json) which are present on disk.
inconsistencies.expected: INDEX_COMPACT should include all active entries from index.json
inconsistencies.actual: SOP-026, SOP-027, SOP-028 missing from INDEX_COMPACT

inconsistencies.description: SOP entries in global INDEX_COMPACT.json and local SOP INDEX_COMPACT.json have 'category: null' for all entries. Other resource types (KB, SCR) have meaningful categories. SOPs lack any categorization.
inconsistencies.expected: Categories assigned to SOPs (e.g., coordination, operations, lifecycle)

inconsistencies.description: SRC entries in global INDEX_COMPACT.json have 'category: null' for all entries. Sources have no categorization despite being diverse (academic, news, financial, government, developer tools).

Script filenames use mixed conventions: some use hyphens (validate-storage.py, test-edge-cases.py), others use underscores (grade_research.py, merge_research.py, kb_validator.py). The index 'name' field uses hyphens consistently but 'filename' matches actual file names.
inconsistencies.actual: Mix of hyphen and underscore conventions in filenames

inconsistencies.description: Scripts SCR-0029 through SCR-0033 use relative paths starting with '../coordination/' in their filename field, while all other scripts use paths relative to storage/scripts/. This makes filename resolution context-dependent.
inconsistencies.actual: 5 entries use '../coordination/' prefix, 49 use local paths

Global SUMMARY.json claims TOOL entry_count=2 but only TOOL-0001 and TOOL-0002 appear in INDEX_COMPACT.json. No dedicated tools index.json found in storage/api-tools/.
missing_references.issue: TOOL entries have no subsystem-level index file

missing_references.issue: DATA entries exist only in storage/data/index.json, not propagated to compact indexes

schema_issues.description: No shared schema definition exists for index entries across subsystems. KB entries have {id, title, date, team, category, tags, status, confidence, builds_on}. Script entries have {id, name, filename, language, category, description, dependencies, added, added_by_team}. SOP entries have {id, title, filename, version, status, description}. This makes cross-subsystem queries impossible without custom logic per type.
schema_issues.recommendation: Define a base schema with common fields {id, title, date, category, description, status} and type-specific extensions.

schema_issues.description: SOP index.json uses duplicate ID values. Both the superseded SOP-012 v1 and active SOP-012 v2 share id='SOP-012'. Same for SOP-016. This breaks ID uniqueness invariant.
schema_issues.recommendation: Use versioned IDs (SOP-012-v1, SOP-012-v2) or remove superseded entries from the active index.

schema_issues.description: The 3-tier index system (index.json, INDEX_COMPACT.json, SUMMARY.json) has no formal specification for which fields each tier must include, nor an automated synchronization mechanism. This is the root cause of most count mismatches and missing entries.
schema_issues.recommendation: Create a single-source-of-truth (index.json) and generate INDEX_COMPACT.json and SUMMARY.json programmatically via auto_index.py. Add a 'last_sync' hash to detect drift.

schema_issues.description: Cross-references in data files use different formats: DATA index uses array of IDs ["KB-0032", "KB-0008"], unified_benchmarks uses path strings ("source": "prototype/tests/benchmark_results.json"), and final_analysis uses dot-notation paths ("unified_benchmarks.prototype_benchmarks"). No consistent cross-reference format.
schema_issues.recommendation: Standardize on a single cross-reference format: {"type": "DATA|KB|SCR|SOP", "id": "ID", "path": "optional.json.path"}.

recommendations.description: Run auto_index.py or equivalent to regenerate INDEX_COMPACT.json and SUMMARY.json from index.json for all subsystems. This fixes INC-001 through INC-003 and ORP-002 through ORP-004. Missing entries: KB-0032 in KB compact, SCR-0051-0054 in scripts compact, SOP-026-028 in SOP compact.
Add KB-0033, SOP-032, and 12+ unregistered script files to their respective index.json files. These files exist on disk but are invisible to any index-based lookup.

Refactor final_analysis.json to reference unified_benchmarks.json and empirical_benchmarks.json by DATA ID and JSON path instead of embedding duplicate values. This eliminates ~16KB of redundant data and prevents future value drift (INC-004).
recommendations.impact: Eliminates 35% storage overhead, prevents value inconsistencies

recommendations.description: Define a base entry schema used across all subsystems. Standardize date field names (use 'date' everywhere), count field names (use 'entry_count'), and cross-reference format. Document in a SCHEMA.json file.
recommendations.impact: Fixes 5 schema issues, enables cross-subsystem tooling

recommendations.description: Resolve duplicate SOP-012 and SOP-016 IDs in SOP index.json. Either use versioned IDs or archive superseded entries separately.
KB-0012 and KB-0013 have identical titles and content about government/open data APIs. Merge KB-0013 into KB-0012 and add a redirect/deprecation notice.
SRC-0018 and SRC-0039 both reference the FRED API. Remove the duplicate and update any references.
Lowercase all tags in KB index.json to prevent duplicates like 'sops' vs 'SOPs'. Merge duplicate tag entries in tag_index (e.g., two 'sqlite' blocks).

Create a pre-commit or periodic check that verifies: (a) all index tiers agree on counts, (b) all disk files are registered, (c) all index entries point to existing files, (d) no duplicate IDs exist. This prevents future drift.
recommendations.impact: Prevents all discovered issues from recurring

recommendations.description: Add run_id and exact_timestamp fields to all benchmark data to distinguish multiple runs of the same test. This resolves the confusion between 3230 vs 3611 ops/s SQLite contention values.
